# scripts/Interaction/Door.gd

[Source:1](../../../../../scripts/Interaction/Door.gd#L1)

Declarations come from source. Unannotated types are explicit; see the [system guides](../../../../systems/README.md) for runtime schemas, nullability, ownership, units and side effects.

Hinged AnimatableBody3D with key/pick lock, swing, navigation, and evidence.
Its origin is the hinge foot; the closed panel runs along +X, front toward
-Z. Body checks stop rotation toward people, ragdolls, and held objects.

Base: `AnimatableBody3D`. Registered class: `Door`.

### _would_hit_body

```gdscript
func _would_hit_body(angle: float, direction: float) -> bool
```

[Source:234](../../../../../scripts/Interaction/Door.gd#L234)

Would the panel push into a PERSON at this angle, or a man lying down (a
body, the limbs of one gone limp), or what you hold in your hands? Crates
and keys on the floor are simply pushed aside: a key on the floor must not
jam a door. Only what is on the side the door swings TOWARD counts;
whoever just opened it is standing against the other face. Static walls
are not checked: a door that swings into a wall is a level bug, not a
runtime one.

| Parameter | Type in source | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `angle` | `float` | required |
| `direction` | `float` | required |

Return type: `bool`.

Internal helper or engine callback; use system entry points for integration.
